contracts.protected_operation: write_file (rewrite/append), create_directory, move_file, delete_file, and edit_block tool executions that mutate the filesystem.
contracts.protected_resource: Local filesystem paths writable by the agent's file-write tools; confined in project mode to the active project root plus extra dirs, otherwise to configured system_tools.file_write.allowed_directories.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent-invoked filesystem mutation tools (write_file, create_directory, move_file, delete_file, edit_block) must validate every target path through validate_write_path before mutating the filesystem, refusing paths outside the effective allowed directories and paths whose extension is in the configured blocked_extensions list.
scope_limits: If no active project root is bound, allowed directories come from config system_tools.file_write.allowed_directories; an empty list disables directory confinement entirely (validate_path_access returns the resolved path unconditionally, _config.py:75-76).
In project mode, relative paths (including '.') resolve against the active project root; effective allowed dirs are project root plus extra dirs (_config.py:53-58, 67-71).
The extension block applies only when blocked_extensions is configured and non-empty (_config.py:104-105).
move_file validates both source and destination through validate_write_path (file_write_tools.py:203-204).
On rejection the tool returns an 'Error: ...' string to the model rather than raising; no filesystem mutation occurs for that call.
The guard is inside these five tool bodies; filesystem writes from any other code path are not covered by it.

contracts.declared_mechanism: _validate_command extracts command names from the full command string (splitting on ; & | separators and $()/backtick subcommand patterns), compares each case-insensitively against system_tools.command.blocked_commands, and returns an error string on match; each tool checks it before Popen and returns 'Error: ...' without spawning.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Spawning a command whose extracted command name equals a blocked_commands entry — case-insensitive exact match, or a match where the extracted name ends with a path separator followed by the blocked name — the condition for which _validate_command returns an error message (command_tools.py:139-143).

contracts.protected_resource: OS process/shell execution initiated by the agent's command tools.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent-invoked shell-execution tools (run_command, start_background_process) must check the supplied command string against the configured blocked_commands blocklist via _validate_command before spawning any process, refusing execution when any extracted command name matches a blocked entry.
scope_limits: The blocklist is inactive when blocked_commands is absent or empty (returns None immediately, command_tools.py:133-136).
Matching is name-extraction-based: exact or path-suffix comparison of the leading token of each command segment; arguments, quoting, and encodings are not analyzed.
Other tools in the module (list_all_processes, kill_process, list_agent_started_processes) execute fixed commands and do not call _validate_command.
On block, the tool returns an error string to the model; no process is spawned for that call.

If interrupt_on ends up empty, no middleware is appended (engine.py:475-476).

The underlying effects of gated tools span other strata (filesystem writes, process spawns) and carry their own in-tool guards covered by separate contracts; this contract covers only the approval gate on tool invocation.
